newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent ends 58 cts up on late short-covering.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent ends 58 cts up on late short-covering.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures closed sharply higher on Tuesday after a late rally fuelled by short-covering on both sides of the Atlantic, brokers said.
April Brent last traded 58 cents up at $19.50 a barrel, off a session high of $19.63 made in the last half hour of trade.
"There were more than a few people who were short and had to come into to cover. They want to have their positions sorted before the APIs come out," said one dealer.
"There's no headlines out there. It's just a short-covering rally," said another.
NYMEX crude also closed strongly at $20.64 a barrel, up 39 cents on the day, having held above the psychologically important $20.00 level.
"(NYMEX) was strong too but the arb came in," a broker said.
Weekly U.S. inventory data from the American Petroleum Institute (API) was due to be released after the close of trade on Tuesday.

Higher imports were seen boosting crude stocks by as much as four million barrels. Distillate stocks were expected to show a seasonal draw of one to two million barrels, while a slight build in gasoline stocks was expected by traders.
Earlier, IPE gas oil closed higher after bargain hunting buyers came into the market to take advantage of recent losses, brokers said.
The March contract settled $3.50 a tonne up at $163.50, having touched a session high of $164.25.
"It was very well supported today, the arb against the States got crushed," said one broker.
Brokers said that fund buyers joined local traders in the market.
